summary: The root "wfr" means to be or make full, complete, abundant, or ample. It applies to things like property, herbage, and even one's honor or dignity.
lane: 1 وَفَرَ ذ , (T, S, M, A, Msb, K,) aor. يَفِرُ ; (T, Msb, K; *) and وَفُرَ , [aor. يَوْفُرُ ;] (A, K;) inf. n. وُفُورٌ (T, S, M, Msb, K) and وَفْرٌ and فِرَةٌ , (M, K,) [all of the former,] or وَفْرٌ is inf. n. of the trans. v.; (Msb;) and وَفَارَةٌ , (K,) [which is of the latter;] It (a thing) was, or became, full, complete, perfect, whole, or entire: (S, Msb:) or it (a thing, TA, or property, M, K, and herbage, M, [and a collection of goods, or commodities, or household furniture and utensils,]) was, or became, much, abundant, ample, or copious; (T, M, A, K;) not deficient: (T:) or it (anything) was, or became, generally, or universally, comprehensive: [syn., in the last sense, عَمَّ , as is implied by an explanation of the epithet وَفْرٌ , by which this sense of the verb is indicated in the lexicons whence this signification is taken:] (M, A, K:) as also , (K,) [and : see وَافِرٌ .] You say also of a branch, وَرَقًا [ It was full of, or abounded with, leaves ]. (L, K, art. غمد . وَفَرَ عِرْضُهُ The text has an illegible third word. , and وَفِرَ , (M, L,) inf. n. [of the former] وُفُورٌ , (M,) (tropical:) [ His honour, dignity, or estimation, was unimpaired; ] he was honourable, or generous, not careless of his honour, or dignity, or estimation. (M, L.) -A2- وَفَرَهُ , (T, S, M, A, Msb, K, *) aor. يَفِرُهُ , (T, Msb,) inf. n. وَفُرٌ (T, S, M, Msb, K) and فِرَةٌ , (T, M,) and وَفْرَةٌ , (TA, as from the K, but wanting in the CK and in a MS. copy of the K,) He made it full, without lack or defect, complete, perfect, whole, or entire; (S, Msb;) as also , inf. n. تَوْفيرٌ ; (K;) and , inf. n. إِيفَارٌ ; and : S, * TA:) or, as also , (T, M, A, K,) which latter is the usual form, (Lth, T,) he made it much, abundant, ample, or copious; (Lth, T, M, A, K;) not deficient. (Lth, T.) You say, وَفَرَ لَهُ مَالَهُ He made his property much, abundant, ample, or copious. (K, * TA.) And it is said in a trad., الحَمْدُ للّٰهِ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَفِرُهُ ٱلْمَنْعُ Praise be to God, whom withholding doth not make to abound. (TA.) You say also, الثَّوْبَ He cut out the garment whole. (M, K.) And السِّقَآءَ He made the skin whole, without cutting off any redundance. (M.) And لَهُ طَعَامَهْ , inf. n. تَوْفِيرٌ , I made his food full, or complete, in quantity; not deficient. (Msb.) And وَفَّرْتُ عَلَيْهِ حَقَّهُ I gave him the whole of his right, or due, and so he received the whole of it; syn. of the former verb with its objective complement and the prep., وَفَّيْتُهُ , (A, Mgh,) or أَعْطَيْتُهُ الجمِيعَ ; (Msb;) and of the latter verb with its objective complement, : (A, Mgh, K:) or both these verbs, thus used, signify the same, i. e., استوفاه , (S, K) [in the former of which we read, وَفَّرَ عَلَيْهِ حَقَّهُ تَوْفيرًا وَٱسْتَوْفَرَهُ أَىِ ٱسْتَوْفَاهُ ; and in the latter, اِسْتَوْفَرَ عَلَيْهِ حَقَّهُ إِسْتَوْفَاهُ كَوَفَّرَهُ .] You also say, وَفَرَهُ عَطَآءَهَ , (M, K,) inf. n. وَفْرٌ , (TA,) He restored, or returned to him his gift, being content with it, (M, K.) or deeming it little. (M, TA.) And وَفَّرَ ٱللّٰهُ حَظَّهُ مِنْ كَذَا God made his lot, or share, of such a thing, full, or complete. (T.) And شَعَرَهُ (tropical:) He left his hair to become abundant and long. (A, TA.) And وَفَرْتُ العِرْضَ , aor. أَفِرُهُ , (Msb,) inf. n. وَفْرٌ (Msb, TA) and فِرَةٌ ; (TA [in my copy of the Msb, افر , which is probably a mistranscription;]) and وَفَّرْتُهُ , in an intensive sense; (Msb;) He preserved, or guarded, honour, dignity, or estimation. (Msb.) And وَفَرَهُ عِرْضَهُ ; (S, M, A, K;) and وفّرهُ عِرْضَهُ ; (A;) and وَفَرَهُ لَهُ ; (M;) or لَهُ , (K,) inf. n. تَوْفِيرٌ ; (TA;) (tropical:) [ He preserved his honour, &c., unimpaired; ] he spoke well of him, and did not find fault with him; (A;) he did not revile him; (M, K;) as though he preserved it [namely his honour, &c.] to him abundant and good, not diminishing it by reviling. (M.) It is said in a proverb, تُوفَرُ وَتُحْمَدُ عَلَى كَذَا (S, * A,) (tropical:) Thy honour, or dignity, or estimation, will be preserved, or guarded, and thou wilt be spoken well of, for such a thing: (A:) from وَفَرْتُهُ عِرْضَهُ ; and مَالَهُ : (S:) said by him to whom a thing is offered: and applied to a man who, when thou hast given to him a thing, returneth it to thee without discontent, or without esteeming it little. (Fr, S.)
